title: Extract minimal prompt metadata; distinguish code targets from prose
context: Task records were capturing too much prompt context and not distinguishing between code-like delivery targets (paths, symbols) and task descriptions (prose phrases). This conflated concerns: task records should index files touched but not preserve arbitrary prompt prose. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_91e6074b66 (Capability pages for functionality shipped in the current release must state that it ships today and must not retain the stale banner 'In development for the next release.'); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Extract only the prompt's first line as task title (72 chars, word-cut; generic fallback for credential-looking prompts). Classify delivery targets with targetLooksLikePath() to separate code artifacts (paths/symbols) from task phrases. Only code-like targets become file anchors in task records.
consequences: hunch_why <file> now also lists read-only tasks that touched the file, enabling cross-linking via delivery targets.
Task records remain lean: no full prompt prose, only brief title and code targets.
Credential-heavy prompts don't leak sensitive strings into task records (generic fallback title).
Task deliveries retain target context for navigation without over-capturing documentation strings.
alternatives_rejected: Record full prompt or task description prose in task records (violates leanness and safety).
Treat all delivery targets identically (blurs distinction between code and documentation).
Keep deliveries without their targets (loses navigation context for hunch_why).
Record every target as file anchor regardless of format (pollutes file index with prose phrases).
